pr.title: Consider empty-unreachable otherwise branches in MatchBranchSimplification
pr.author: clubby789

issues.title: [MIR-opt] `matches!(x, Some(_))` should simplify to `Eq(Discriminant, Const)`

processing.reason: The historical behavior in PR #131244 is a missed optimization, not a semantic miscompile. Before the fix, SimplifyToIf rejected a SwitchInt with two explicit values plus an empty-unreachable otherwise block (`targets.iter().len() != 1`), leaving the original switchInt/branch CFG intact. The old and new programs therefore compute exactly the same result for every input; only the number of basic blocks changes. Encoding the unoptimized switch as the "transformed" function would produce identical return values on all tested inputs, so no source-grounded counterexample with differing original/transformed outputs exists. Forcing a value difference would invent semantics not present in the PR.

analysis.summary: MatchBranchSimplification's SimplifyToIf previously required exactly one explicit switch value (`targets.iter().len() != 1`), so exhaustive two-value switches whose fallback block is empty-unreachable were left as multi-block switchInts. The fix treats the second explicit target as the `otherwise` target when the real fallback `bbs[otherwise].is_empty_unreachable()`, allowing `matches!(x, Some(_))` to collapse to a discriminant comparison (`Ne`). This is a missed-optimization bug fix, not a miscompile.
analysis.originalLogic: `SimplifyToIf::can_simplify` only accepted a `SwitchInt` with exactly one explicit value plus the fallback: `if targets.iter().len() != 1 { return None; }`, then selected `let (_, first) = targets.iter().next().unwrap(); let second = targets.otherwise();`. `apply` mirrored this with `let (val, first) = targets.iter().next().unwrap(); let second = targets.otherwise();`. Thus a switch with two explicit values (e.g. `[0: bb2, 1: bb3, otherwise: bb1]`) was rejected even when `bb1` was `unreachable;`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically wrong behavior was a failure to apply the simplification: for a `SwitchInt` with two explicit values and an empty-unreachable fallback, the pass returned `None` and preserved the five-block `switchInt`/branch structure instead of folding it into a discriminant comparison. It was not an incorrect code rewrite. The corrected logic pairs `&[first, second, otherwise]` with a fallback satisfying `bbs[otherwise].is_empty_unreachable()`, using `second` as the fallback-equivalent branch and discarding the unreachable block.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR `SwitchInt` terminators on a discriminant where either (a) there is exactly one explicit value plus fallback, or (b) there are exactly two explicit values plus a fallback block whose body is empty and `unreachable;`, with distinct targets and branch bodies eligible for `SimplifyToIf` (e.g. both branches assign constants). Canonical example: `match bar { Some(_) => true, None => false }` on `Option<()>`, producing `switchInt(move _2) -> [0: bb2, 1: bb3, otherwise: bb1]` with `bb1: { unreachable; }`.
analysis.trigger: A `SwitchInt` has two explicit values and an `otherwise` target whose block is empty-unreachable (for example, an exhaustive two-variant `Option`/enum match such as `matches!(x, Some(_))`), so the old `targets.iter().len() != 1` guard prevents simplification.
preconditions: The switch has either exactly one explicit value or exactly two explicit values plus a fallback in `all_targets()`.
In the two-explicit-value case, `bbs[otherwise].is_empty_unreachable()` must hold for the fallback block.
The selected `first` and `second` target blocks must be distinct (`if first == second { return None; }`).
`all_values()` arity must match: one value for `[first, otherwise]`, two values for `[first, second, otherwise]`.
The branch bodies must satisfy the `SimplifyToIf` structural checks (e.g. constant true/false assignments) before replacing the switch with a comparison.
`apply` must choose the same value/target/otherwise pairing as `can_simplify`; its new `_ => unreachable!()` assumes the prior check succeeded.
pitfalls: Treating `targets.iter().len() != 1` as sufficient excludes exhaustive two-value switches with unreachable fallbacks.

When two explicit values exist, the second explicit target must be used as `second`; using the unreachable fallback block as `second` would be wrong and can leave an unreachable branch in the rewritten CFG.

Accepting two explicit values without confirming the real fallback is empty-unreachable would be semantically wrong: values other than the explicit ones would incorrectly be routed to the second branch.
Do not drop the distinctness check: `first == second` must still reject the rewrite.
Keep `all_targets()` (includes fallback) and `all_values()` (excludes fallback) arities aligned; mismatched slicing should not be accepted.
Preserve comparison orientation: `[0: false, 1: true]` with unreachable fallback becomes `Ne(discr, 0)`, not a swapped `Eq`/constant.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a focused `tests/mir-opt/matches_reduce_branches.rs` case `my_is_some(bar: Option<()>) -> bool` with `EMIT_MIR ...MatchBranchSimplification.diff`, `CHECK: = Ne`, and `CHECK: return`, plus call it from `main` as the patch does. The expected diff must show the old five-block switch (`switchInt ... [0: bb2, 1: bb3, otherwise: bb1]`, `bb1: { unreachable; }`) replaced by a single block computing `Ne(copy _3, const 0_isize)`. Update dependent MIR expectations such as `issue_59352.num_to_digit` where the same pattern now folds. Add negative coverage for a switch with two explicit values but a reachable/non-empty fallback, and confirm the original one-explicit-value path still simplifies.
